greek.forms: Singular: κόσμος, κόσμου, κόσμῳ, κόσμον, κόσμε. Plural: κόσμοι, κόσμων, κόσμοις, κόσμους
greek.etymology: From root meaning 'to arrange/order'. English descendants: Cosmos (the universe as ordered whole), Cosmetic (relating to beautification/ornament), Cosmopolitan (citizen of the world), Cosmonaut (universe sailor, Russian borrowing). The semantic shift from 'ornament' to 'universe' reflects Greek view of cosmic order. The word originally meant 'arrangement' or 'ornament.'
greek.literary_context: Heraclitus, Fragment 30, preserved by Clement of Alexandria
greek.usage_example: κόσμον τόνδε, τὸν αὐτὸν ἁπάντων — This cosmos, which is the same for all
greek.did_you_know: Ancient Greek women wore elaborate hair ornaments called κόσμοι (KOS-moy) - the same word used for the universe! The connection wasn't coincidental: Greeks saw beauty in both personal adornment and cosmic arrangement, believing the same principles of harmony governed both.
